items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: I agreed to give Jacques co-authorship of the song and the copyright, although actually it was my song.

ctx.x: Definitely not. In fact I didn't get any money at all. I got paid for the date and I didn't get any money for -- which is a sad part of my life. But unfortunately I wasn't a good businessman and you know, in this business they always tell you you have to make a name for yourself. Even now people are telling me, rather than to offer you a decent salary they tell you that you have to get known, you know, or you have to have a hit records or some-thing.

And unfortunately for me the song that I wrote that was a hit, that wasn't recorded under my name, and it was a controversy about who wrote it because I agreed to give Jacques co-authorship of the song and the copyright, although actually it was my song. And so consequently a lot of people were not aware of the fact that I am the composer of "Robin's Nest," you see.
